articles.title: Morning recap
articles.summary:
Morning recap

Good morning, Middle East Eye readers,

If you're just joining us, here are key developments:

• President Donald Trump said US and Iranian representatives had met for "very good" talks at the United Nations, hours after he threatened Iran with "annihilation".

• Special envoy Steve Witkoff said the US had "engaged in lengthy talks" with the Iranian delegation through the mediators who "shuttled between the two sides throughout the day".

• Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei has said that Tehran engaged with the US through a Qatari mediator in New York and conveyed its conditions, including an end to the war on all fronts and a halt to "acts of aggression", state news agency IRNA reported.

• Colombia has withdrawn its Article 63 declaration of intervention in South Africa’s Gaza genocide case against Israel, according to the International Court of Justice.

• Power supply lines were damaged and there was a complete power outage in Lebanon's Nabaa al-Hamas area after an Israeli air strike targeted al-Khiam in southern Lebanon overnight. 

• A Palestinian was killed, and three others were injured, late on Tuesday night in Israeli shelling near al-Nafaq Street, east of Gaza City.

•  The Canadian and Croatian prime ministers, and the Angolan president, joined a chorus of world leaders who have condemned genocide against Palestinians and called for a two-state solution at the UN General Assembly.

• Three commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, down from four a day earlier and below the 10-day moving average of about 15.

• Oil prices fell on Wednesday after Trump said US and Iranian representatives met for "very good" talks at the United Nations.

•  The two-state solution is the only credible path to lasting peace and security for Palestinians, Israelis and the wider region, UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres has said.

•  Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura terminal recorded its busiest loading day since before the war on 21 September, as six very large crude carriers (VLCCs) lifted close to 12m barrels at Ras Tanura and Juaymah.

articles.title: Report: Hormuz traffic on Tuesday below 10-day average
articles.summary:
Report: Hormuz traffic on Tuesday below 10-day average

Three commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, down from four a day earlier and below the 10-day moving average of about 15, preliminary shipping data showed on Wednesday.

The figures may change as some ships typically switch off their transponders during the voyage.
All three vessels, including one Panamax tanker, were exiting the strait, the data from shiptracker Kpler showed at 0200 GMT.

One ballast liquefied natural gas tanker, Al Mafyar, however reappeared inside the strait on Tuesday, after being last seen outside of the waterway on September 19, according to both Kpler and LSEG data.

The Strait of Hormuz carried a fifth of the world's oil and gas before the US-Iran conflict.
Meanwhile, 22 commodity vessels transited the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on Tuesday, another maritime chokepoint on the southwest tip of Yemen and a vital trade route for oil between the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.

The data showed 14 vessels heading towards the Red Sea and 8 towards the Gulf of Aden. 
The number compared with an average of around 26 ships using the strait in the past 10 days.

Report by Reuters

articles.title: Oil prices fall after Trump hails 'very productive' US-Iran talks at UN
articles.summary:
Oil prices fall after Trump hails 'very productive' US-Iran talks at UN

Oil prices fell on Wednesday after President Donald Trump said US and Iranian representatives had met for "very good" talks at the United Nations.

The international benchmark, Brent crude, and main US contract, West Texas Intermediate, dipped to $98.91 and $89.93 per barrel respectively in early Asian trade -- well below the symbolic $100 mark they have smashed repeatedly since the Middle Eat war broke out in February.

The three-hour meeting was "very good", "very productive" and "they have another one scheduled in the very near future", Trump told reporters as he met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Trump's announcement came just hours after he delivered a bellicose address to the UN in which he said he faced a "big decision" on whether to make a deal with Iran or "annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly".

Report by AFP

articles.title: Kpler: Saudi terminal's busiest loading day points to 'changing vessel behaviour'
articles.summary:
Kpler: Saudi terminal's busiest loading day points to 'changing vessel behaviour'

Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura terminal recorded its busiest loading day since before the war on 21 September, as six very large crude carriers (VLCCs) lifted close to 12 million barrels at Ras Tanura and Juaymah, according to analytics firm Kpler.

The surge followed disruption to the kingdom's East-West pipeline, which normally allows Saudi crude to bypass the Strait of Hormuz altogether by moving oil overland to the Red Sea coast. 

Kpler's analysts say some of the six vessels involved in the loading surge had already been flagged for dark ship-to-ship transfers or unusual port calls in the previous six weeks, suggesting the rerouting seen on 21 September “sits on top of a longer-running pattern of changing vessel behaviour”.

Ras Tanura just recorded its busiest loading day since before the war.
